title: Unprefixed Variable-Length Array Parsing (UNPREFIXED_ARRAY_PARSING)
pattern: Parsing variable-length byte blocks or string slices by scanning sequentially for a sentinel terminator byte (e.g., null-termination) instead of using an explicit length prefix.
why_bad: If the sentinel terminator byte is corrupted, missing, or omitted by a faulty transmitter, the parser will read past the allocated buffer bounds. This leads to crashes, buffer overflows, or severe security read violations (CWE-125/CWE-787).
detection: Look for while/for loops that read sequentially from raw byte indices until a sentinel byte is found, without performing safe length bounds checks against the buffer.
fix: Adopt length-prefixed (Pascal-style) variable-size layout packing, validating the buffer capacity upfront before starting sequential array reads.
source: *Alex Petrov - Database Internals (2019)*, Chapter 3 (Strings and Variable-Size Data); *Paul McKenney - Is Parallel Programming Hard (Perfbook, 2019)*, Chapter 13.
